raw_response:
Thirty years on this land, so I know what works here in Quzhou. My farm is small — 4.1 mu total — so every bag of fertilizer I buy, I feel it. My kids mostly work in Shijiazhuang now, but my wife and one son help me during transplanting and harvest.

I split my land the same way I did last year: about 2 mu for cotton, the rest — 2.1 mu — for stevia. The stevia company I contract with picks up my dried leaves in September, which gives me a steadier income than cotton alone. Cotton prices jump around too much.

**Cotton (2 mu):** I've been using the same Bt hybrid the dealer in town sells for five years now. Works fine, and Lao Wang next to me uses it too. I plough before planting because that field has been in cotton a long time and gets hard. For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound 15-15-15 per mu as base — that's 7.5 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium per mu. Then I topdress with about half a bag of urea per mu during squaring and boll setting, which adds another 11.5 kg nitrogen. Total nitrogen comes to around 19 kg per mu. I know the extension people say to split it more carefully, but I've done it this way for years and my yields are okay. I irrigate 4 times: before planting, at squaring, at boll setting, and one more in late August if it's dry. Bollworm and aphids need spraying — I go through 6 rounds of pesticide by October. I expect around 210 kg seed cotton per mu. Last year I got 200, the year before 220, so 210 is what I plan for.

**Stevia (2.1 mu):** The company gives me their improved transplants to buy — I don't use my own seed. Stevia doesn't need as heavy fertilizer as cotton. I apply one bag of compound 15-15-15 per mu as base, then maybe 0.3 bags of urea per mu when the plants are putting out new growth — about 14 kg nitrogen per mu total. Phosphorus and potassium come mostly from the compound fertilizer, about 7–8 kg per mu each. I use the rotary machine for tillage here, no need to plough deep. Stevia leaves need steady moisture so I irrigate 5 times through the season. Pests are lighter — aphids and whitefly mostly — so I spray 3 times. I expect 160 kg of dried leaf per mu. The company said 180 is possible with their new variety but I'll say 160 to be safe.

My total fertilizer cost will be around 600–700 yuan. That's tight but manageable since my son sends money home every month. I'm not changing anything big this year — change is risky on a small farm.
